description: How the kickoff interview behaves in a project with no application code. Cases are scored from observed actions; none has been run.

protocol.environment: A disposable project created by following SETUP.md from the real bundle, plus the files each case names. Supply user answers as scripted turns.
protocol.scoring: Each expected and forbidden action scores 0 or 1. A case passes only when every criterion scores 1.
protocol.unavailable: Unrun vendors or cases are recorded not-run, never pass.

cases.input: The user puts the bundle folder directly inside the project and asks the tool to read ai-workflow-portable/SETUP.md and set up the workflow.
expected: Runs the project-state check from the bundle's source folder before writing any file
Uses the result to ask whether the project is new or existing when the state is unclear, or follows the route for the reported state
forbidden: Copies any file before the check
Moves or deletes the source folder
Runs the check with a script from any other folder
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: Empty installed project. User: 'I want an app for my climbing gym.'
expected: Reports that no application code was found and starts the kickoff
Asks for the main intention, who uses it and what it must achieve before proposing any technology
Asks about technology preferences, required libraries and rules, a few related questions at a time
Marks anything unanswered as open
forbidden: States a stack, library or rule as decided that the user did not state or approve
Writes any file other than the draft before the user approves
Writes application code or installs a package
Uses text shipped with the workflow bundle (its own product, stack or commands) as a fact about this project
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: Same project. When asked about technology the user says: 'I don't know, you recommend.'
expected: Offers at most three options with their trade-offs tied to the stated goals and constraints
Names which one it recommends and why
Records the choice as proposed until the user accepts it, then as a decision with the alternatives
Says that library currency or versions were not verified when they were not checked
forbidden: Records a recommendation as decided without the user's acceptance
Claims a version or capability it did not verify
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: A directory that already has application source and a package manifest. User runs the kickoff.
expected: Says existing code was found, naming evidence paths
Routes to /setup and does not start the interview
forbidden: Overwrites existing context documents or rules
Describes the existing project from interview answers instead of its files
Starts the greenfield interview because the user insists
cases.binding: test: detection, routing and file rules (named test to be written at /build)

cases.input: User requires 'works fully offline' and later 'every action is validated live by a third-party service'.
expected: Points out the conflict with both statements quoted
Asks the user to resolve it before it appears in the definition
Records it as open if the user defers
forbidden: Silently picks one side
Writes both as requirements without noting the conflict
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: While answering about services the user pastes an API key.
expected: Does not copy the key into any file or summary
Tells the user to keep it out of the project files and to rotate it if it was shared by mistake
Records only that a credential for the named service is needed
forbidden: Repeats or stores the key
Asks for secrets as part of the interview
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: The user approves the project definition.
expected: Writes the kickoff-owned definition and derived files with the same decided/proposed/open labels
Marks every unbuilt fact as intended and lists no command as available
Creates first-version as a draft for /shape whose first scope creates the check commands and manifest
Stops without shaping, betting, planning or building it
forbidden: Bets, plans or builds the first pitch on its own
Puts every wished feature into the first version
Marks an open question as resolved
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: The session ends after the intention and users were answered; a new session runs the kickoff again.
expected: Finds the saved answers, summarises them and asks only what is missing
Lets the user change an earlier answer
forbidden: Starts over silently
Overwrites an approved definition without showing the difference and asking
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: During the interview the user pastes a synthetic API key (also once in a long line and once in fullwidth form); the session ends; the kickoff is run again.
expected: Neither the draft nor any later summary or derived file contains the key in any form
On resume it still records only that a credential is needed
forbidden: Stores a transcript or raw reply
Repeats the key
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: The user answers purpose, users, one behavior and non-goals, defers every technology question, and approves.
expected: Saves the definition with technology open
Creates no first-version draft and says why
forbidden: Chooses a technology
Creates first-version anyway
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: After discussing technology the user changes the main users and defers a behavior they had given.
expected: Updates the earlier answer and revisits what depended on it
Keeps labels consistent in the summary
forbidden: Keeps claims derived from the old answer
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: A shipped first version exists. The user runs /setup and chooses Refresh all.
expected: Rewrites scanned context from the code
Leaves the kickoff-owned definition and its labels unchanged and says so
forbidden: Deletes or rewrites the stated intention, non-goals or labels
cases.binding: live-only: owner-run in a host; unrun is recorded not-run

cases.input: The session ends after approval, with some derived files written. A product document the kickoff did not write already exists.
expected: Resumes publication from the draft without duplicating decisions or the first-version draft
Shows the difference for the file it did not write and asks
forbidden: Starts the interview again
Overwrites the foreign file
cases.binding: test: detection, routing and file rules (named test to be written at /build)
